reading.title: Reading a structural model
reading.text: At a supervised education display, Karim studies a building model rather than enters a working site. The foundation transfers loads into the ground. A column is vertical; a beam spans horizontally. A wall may divide spaces, while a floor provides a level surface and a roof covers the building. The staircase connects levels, and the elevator shaft is the vertical space for an elevator. A load-bearing wall supports loads as well as enclosing space. A truss is a framework of connected members. The display compares concrete, steel, brick, glass and timber. Karim asks a qualified guide how the materials serve different functions. He does not infer a structure's safety from its color or copy the model as a construction plan.

reading.title: Discussing stages and materials
reading.text: Karim reads a supervised tour's schedule. Stone and aluminum are material names; insulation limits heat transfer, and drywall forms interior surfaces. Rebar reinforces concrete. Excavation removes ground before foundation work. Pouring foundation refers here to placing concrete for the foundation, while framing creates the building's supporting framework. Roofing forms or covers the roof. Plumbing concerns water and drainage systems; electrical is used here for electrical-system work. Drywall installation precedes finishing and painting. Flooring concerns the floor finish. Inspection means examining work against relevant requirements. The guide emphasizes that this vocabulary list is not a universal sequence or instruction manual. Skilled people coordinate the activities, and conditions, regulations and project designs determine the actual work.

reading.title: Matching professional responsibilities
reading.text: A fictional project meeting assigns responsibilities without treating them as interchangeable. The general contractor coordinates the building work, and a foreman supervises a work crew. A carpenter works with wood; an electrician works with electrical systems. A plumber handles water and drainage systems, and a mason works with brick or stone. An ironworker erects or installs structural steel and related metal components. A crane operator operates lifting equipment, while a surveyor measures and establishes site positions. A safety inspector examines conditions against safety requirements. Karim checks the stated responsibility before contacting someone. A hard hat or tool in a photograph cannot establish a person's qualifications. Actual authority, licensing and responsibilities depend on local rules and the project's arrangements.
